question: A copper wire of cross-sectional area $2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$ carries a current of $4.0\text{ A}$. The number density of free electrons is $8.0 \times 10^{28}\text{ m}^{-3}$. A length $0.25\text{ m}$ of this wire is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of $0.20\text{ T}$. Calculate the drift speed of electrons and the magnetic force on this part of the wire.

options.A: $v_d=\dfrac{I}{neA}=\dfrac{4.0}{8.0\times10^{28}\times1.6\times10^{-19}\times2.0\times10^{-6}}=1.56\times10^{-4}\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Since wire is perpendicular to $B$, $F=BIl=0.20\times4.0\times0.25=0.20\text{ N}$.
options.C: $v_d=1.56\times10^{-4}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $F=0$ because wire is perpendicular to field.
